# Type URI Design

Covers Dimension 3: How teams structure type URIs for problem details.

See [citations.md](../citations.md) for full source details.

## RFC Requirements

The `type` member is a URI reference identifying the problem category [1]:

- Defaults to `about:blank` when absent [1]
- Absolute URIs recommended over relative to prevent confusion [1] [17]
- Consumers MUST use the type URI as the primary problem identifier [1]
- Consumers SHOULD NOT automatically dereference the type URI [1]
- If resolvable (http/https), dereferencing SHOULD provide human-readable
  documentation [1]

## URI Scheme Options

| Scheme | Resolvable | Example | Used By |
|--------|-----------|---------|---------|
| https:// | Yes | `https://example.com/probs/out-of-credit` | RFC 9457 examples [1] |
| http:// | Yes | `http://example.com/errors/not-found` | General guidance [1] |
| urn: | No | `urn:problem-type:belgif:resourceNotFound` | Belgian government [15] |
| tag: | No | `tag:example.com,2025:problems:service/error` | RFC 4151 option [1] |
| about: | N/A | `about:blank` | Default [1] |

RFC 9457 encourages resolvable URIs "because it might become desirable to
resolve the URI in the future" [1].

## Real-World Patterns

### Pattern 1: Resolvable HTTPS URIs

Used by RFC 9457's own examples [1]:

```
https://example.com/probs/out-of-credit
```

Advantages: can host documentation at the URI. Requires maintaining the URI
endpoint.

### Pattern 2: Non-Resolvable URIs with External Documentation

Used by Zalando [23] [22]:

- Type URIs are non-dereferenceable
- Documentation lives in the OpenAPI specification instead
- Mandated for all 4xx and 5xx responses (Rule #176) [23]
- Adds flow ID extension for microservice tracing [22]

### Pattern 3: URN-Based Identifiers

Used by Belgian government (BelgIF) [15]:

```
urn:problem-type:belgif:resourceNotFound
urn:problem-type:belgif:badRequest
urn:problem-type:belgif:tooManyRequests
```

Advantages: stable across environments, no hosting requirement, semantic
meaning in the identifier structure [15].

### Pattern 4: IANA Registry Prefix

For standardized types [2]:

```
https://iana.org/assignments/http-problem-types#date
https://iana.org/assignments/http-problem-types#ohttp-key
```

Limited to truly universal problem types — vendor-specific, application-specific,
and deployment-specific values cannot be registered [2].

### Pattern 5: Vendor Problem Registry

SmartBear maintains a public problems registry [11]:

```
https://problems-registry.smartbear.com/missing-body-property
https://problems-registry.smartbear.com/invalid-body-property-format
https://problems-registry.smartbear.com/missing-request-parameter
```

Provides reusable problem types via SwaggerHub domains [10] [11].

### Pattern 6: Auto-Generated from Class Name

Used by the rfc9457 Python library [8]:

```python
class UserNotFoundError(NotFoundProblem):
    title = "User not found."
# type becomes: "user-not-found"
```

Simple but produces non-URI type values that don't conform to the RFC's
guidance for http/https scheme [1].

## Namespacing

The type URI serves as the natural namespace for extension members [1].
Common organizational patterns observed in the wild:

- By domain: `/authentication/`, `/authorization/`, `/validation/`
- By service: `/orders/`, `/payments/`, `/users/`
- By error category: `/client/`, `/server/`, `/external/`

## Versioning

RFC 9457 does not define a versioning strategy for type URIs [1]. The type
URI should be stable over time — it identifies the error class, not the
specific occurrence [1]. API versioning strategies (URI path, header-based,
query parameter) are orthogonal to problem type URI design.

## Comparison with Non-RFC 9457 Approaches

| API | Error Identifier | Format |
|-----|-----------------|--------|
| Stripe | `type` enum + `code` string [12] | Custom (not URI-based) |
| GitHub | `errors[].code` string [13] | Custom (not URI-based) |
| Google Cloud | `reason` + `domain` pair [14] | Protobuf ErrorInfo |
| Cloudflare | `type` URI + `error_code` [3] | RFC 9457 compliant |

## Gaps and Limitations

- No consensus on whether type URIs should be resolvable or non-resolvable
- No standard versioning strategy for type URIs when error semantics change
- The rfc9457 Python library generates non-URI type values by default [8]
- Limited data on what percentage of production APIs provide documentation
  at type URIs vs using non-resolvable URIs
